products.content_plain: Of Galician origin and popular throughout the country, these peppers are characterized by their small size, green color and conical shape. Its most curious aspect is the intense spicy flavor that only some have, hence the saying that "some Padrón peppers are hot and others are not." It is something invaluable until you try it, since there are no visible differences between them. These peppers have a nutritional value very similar to that of green peppers. Its main component is water, so its caloric intake is minimal. However, if they are fried in plenty of oil, the calories increase, not because of the peppers, but because of the absorption of oil. Raw, these peppers are an excellent source of vitamin C, but this is not the usual way to consume them. Fried or grilled they lose much of it. Its content of vitamin A and E stands out, and potassium and magnesium are abundant among its minerals. It is recommended not to consume these peppers for people with delicate stomachs since, although not all of them are spicy, the chances that some of them will do so are high. We present these peppers to you in bags of about 300 g, the ideal size to prepare a good portion.

Kg of Padrón pepper, of Galician origin and popular throughout the country, these peppers are characterized by their small size, green color and conical shape. Its most curious aspect is the intense spicy flavor that only some have, hence the saying that "some Padrón peppers are hot and others are not." It is something invaluable until you try it, since there are no visible differences between them. These peppers have a nutritional value very similar to that of green peppers. Its main component is water, so its caloric intake is minimal. However, if they are fried in plenty of oil, the calories increase, not because of the peppers, but because of the absorption of oil. Raw, these peppers are an excellent source of vitamin C, but this is not the usual way to consume them. Fried or grilled they lose much of it. Its content of vitamin A and E stands out, and potassium and magnesium are abundant among its minerals. It is recommended not to consume these peppers for people with delicate stomachs since, although not all of them are spicy, the chances that some of them will do so are high.

The cinnamon color makes it very easy to identify this gourmet bean, with an elongated, rounded shape and medium size. When cooked, its cinnamon color transforms into a beautiful orange-brown. It is the finest and most flavorful of all colored beans, it cooks quickly, does not fall apart, and forms a very creamy broth with a very good flavor. It is grown in the Leonese moor and in Zamora.
White kidney beans are soft and fine on the palate, famous for their butteriness and very thin skin. They are medium-sized, whitish in color with a kidney shape and delicious.

The pinto bean is quite large in size, rounded in shape and pinkish in color with maroon spots. Widely used in typical northern stews, such as Galician broth, when cooked it does not fall apart, its skin is smooth and soft, it gives the broth a dark, creamy color and a strong flavor. It is grown in the lands of La Bañeza in León.
The Pedrosillano chickpea, or pardal peak chickpea, is small and almost spherical, orange-yellow in color, with a small, sharp beak and a very characteristic and delicious flavor.

The pardina lentil is small in diameter (between 3.5 and 4.5 mm) and has a very characteristic brown color, a softer skin than other varieties, a more consistent texture so it does not fall apart when cooked, and a very fine flavor on the palate. Its great richness in protein and its high fiber content make it an excellent dish to maintain a balanced diet. They are grown in the León region of Los Oteros and in the neighboring provinces of Palencia, Valladolid and Zamora, lands of hilly plains, “Tierra de Campos”.
